item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to the Press
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Joint Base Andrews

Secretary of State Marco Rubio Remarks to the Press

Remarks

October 5, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Hey, guys, sorry to be late.  We’ve got to be quick.  Let’s go. 

QUESTION:  Can you talk about —

QUESTION:  Mr. Secretary, why did bombers leave Fairford?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  What?

QUESTION:  Why did American bombers leave Fairford?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, you’ll have to – the Department of War is constantly reallocating resources where they need to be.  There’s regular rotations that happen as well, so I think you guys are just —

QUESTION:  Is there a threat?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, I mean, we’ve documented what happened last week.  I wouldn’t directly tie that to the move that was made.  The only reason why you guys are focused on how many planes are at Fairford is because of the threat that happened last week, but it’s not unusual to see rotations happen and movement of assets to different parts of the world based on exercises, redeployments, people changing out and new people coming in, new planes coming in, old planes going out.  So crews are changing all the time.  You guys are just really focused on that now because of the threat last week.

QUESTION:  So you still have confidence in British security at the base in general?  You —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Oh, we have confidence in the security of all of our bases, because all of our bases are theoretically – could be threatened at any moment, and that’s why there’s so much security built around them.  And with the Brits, we’ve worked very closely for a very long time, including on this investigation, and they couldn’t be more cooperative.

QUESTION:  Mr. Secretary, you’re going to Iceland obviously today.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  We are?  Nobody told me that.  (Laughter.) 

QUESTION:  Albuquerque, not Iceland. 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah.

QUESTION:  Why are you picking Iceland?  And what —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  They’re a NATO member —

QUESTION:  What do you aim to do over there?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah.  Look, they’re a NATO member and have been a good friend of the United States, so it’s an opportunity to stop there and meet with them.  And it’s something that I don’t think has happened in a while.  So – but it really is a result of a conversation I had with their leaders at the NATO Summit – with the leaders earlier this year and with their foreign minister, so I’m looking forward to it.  And I’ve been there before and I don’t know when the last time a Secretary of State went.  It may have been a while, but —

QUESTION:  2021.

QUESTION:  Was the decision made to send —

QUESTION:  Can you speak —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  2021?  All right, not that long ago.

QUESTION:  — air support into Saudis for (inaudible) —

QUESTION:  Wait, wait, hold on a second.  Let’s stay with the trip for a moment, if we could.  So I mean, Portugal and Greece are also NATO members.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah.

QUESTION:  So can you talk a little bit about those two —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, if you go to Europe you’re probably going to go see a NATO member, because most of the countries in Europe are.  In the case of Portugal, they’ve been a strong ally, again, and we have an opportunity to go there and visit with them.  And of course Greece is a very important U.S. ally.  It’s a place that we have not just a military presence but strong economic ties, so it’s an opportunity to go there and see them.

QUESTION:  Can you give us an update on the suspected plague case in Russia?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, we don’t – we know what we know, obviously, about whatever the Russians have provided, which is it seems that there was a worker at the lab that was infected, and there’s concern that that could have spread, at least internally.  So you’ve seen them do quarantines with this – of that nature.  There’s very limited travel between the U.S. and Russia, obviously.  But like anything else, something like that gets out, it could quickly spread.  So we’re watching and monitoring it closely.  I don’t think it’s cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause to just keep an eye on it, and we’re doing that.

QUESTION:  Has a decision been made —

QUESTION:  What’s your view of the offensive this past weekend in the recent days by the Yemeni Government forces and the Saudi forces against the Houthis in Yemen?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  So what’s the question?

QUESTION:  The strikes by the – the counterstrikes by the official Yemeni Government and the Saudi – with Saudi support against the Houthis —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Yeah.

QUESTION:  What’s your view?

QUESTION:  Will the U.S. aid provide air support?

QUESTION:  Or is it coordinated with the U.S.?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, first of all the United States – just on the question of aid, the United States has a defense and security agreement with Saudi Arabia and we intend to live by it.  I won’t discuss details further than that.  As far as our view of it, well, I think it’s – the Saudis and Yemeni forces clearly are not in favor of the Houthis controlling that territory close to the – to the strait there.  And it’s territory that was gained as a result of a Houthi offensive, and this is the counter to it.  We expected that would happen and that’s what’s happening.

So obviously the Saudis have come under Houthi attack and see the threat that that poses, and they have a right to defend themselves.  And obviously the Yemeni forces are going to try to retake territory that they were ousted from.

We’ve got to get going.  We’re late.  So two more. 

QUESTION:  But the Saudis are —

QUESTION:  Okay.  Can you tell us anything —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  What? 

QUESTION:  — about (inaudible) Camp David meeting?  Any decision was made? 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  About what?

QUESTION:  The Camp David meeting on Friday.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  This weekend?

QUESTION:  Yeah.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Oh, we constantly are meeting for long-term strategic planning and things of this nature.  It’s not unusual for us as a team to get together.  That was just an opportunity to do it in a setting where there were less distractions, but we’re constantly – that’s just part of the role the National Security Council plays —

QUESTION:  Yeah.

SECRETARY RUBIO:  — is to bring together stakeholders to sort of do long-term planning – six months, nine months, but in many cases five or 10 years down the road.  So I wouldn’t call it routine because the topics being discussed are global by nature ,but they are long-term in thinking.  So we’ve had many meetings like that before.  This one just happened to be in Camp David —

QUESTION:  (Off-mike.) 

QUESTION:  Brazil – do you have a reaction for the election in Brazil?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, it’s going to a second round.  I think everybody expected that it would, so we’ll see how that plays out.

Last one.

QUESTION:  Mr. Secretary, Russia is calling, urging foreign diplomats —

SECRETARY RUBIO:  You got everybody else?  He’s already had a question.  All right, go —

QUESTION:  Well, on the Houthis, sir —

QUESTION:  Urging – Russia is urging foreign diplomats in Kyiv to leave the town.  What is the U.S.’s position on that?

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, they’ve done that now for months.  Look, we have an embassy presence there, and we’ll make the determination about whether it’s safe for them to be there or not, but that’s not – I mean, they’ve been saying that now for months.  They’ve been warning diplomats to leave for months, and I don’t think it’s a surprise to anyone that Kyiv is under attack.  I think that’s well understood.  But we analyze every single day the safety of every diplomatic mission in the world, and if a threat arises that we feel needs to be addressed by a change in posture, we’ll do so.  We haven’t done that up to this point there.  Okay?  Let’s go.

QUESTION:  Thank you.

item.title: Lesotho National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Lesotho National Day

Press Statement

October 4, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend my congratulations to His Majesty King Letsie III and the people of Lesotho as you commemorate 60 years of independence.

This milestone anniversary is an opportunity to celebrate the enduring partnership between our two nations. The United States remains committed to strengthening our commercial ties through strategic investments such as Convalt Energy’s $6.2 billion hydropower and data center project while also building on the close cooperation we share in health and security.

As you mark this historic occasion, please accept my warmest wishes on behalf of the American people.

item.title: U.S. Statement on Increased Tensions Between Ethiopia and Eritrea
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

U.S. Statement on Increased Tensions Between Ethiopia and Eritrea

Press Statement

October 3, 2026

Increasing cross-border tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea have the potential to affect the entire region.  The Horn of Africa cannot sustain another military conflict and humanitarian crisis.  A conflict jeopardizes ongoing U.S. collaboration on shared interests with both countries.

We strongly urge Ethiopia and Eritrea to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of their neighbors, exercise maximum restraint and return to dialogue and cooperation as agreed in their 2018 peace framework.  Peace through dialogue is the only path toward sustainable security, economic growth, and prosperity.

item.title: Iraq’s National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Iraq’s National Day

Press Statement

October 3, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Iraq on their National Day on October 3.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s July visit to Washington and his meeting with President Trump at the White House reaffirmed the close friendship between our two nations and our shared commitment to a strong and prosperous future.  The historic economic partnerships announced during the visit further demonstrate the tremendous potential for cooperation between American and Iraqi businesses.  We also welcome Iraq’s efforts to strengthen its sovereignty and contribute to security and stability across the region.  

On this National Day, we celebrate the history, resilience, and achievements of the Iraqi people and look forward to the continued growth and partnership between our two nations.  We extend our warmest wishes to the people of Iraq as they commemorate this important occasion.

item.title: Germany National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Germany National Day

Press Statement

October 3, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the German people as you mark the 36th anniversary of German Unity on October 3.

The peaceful reunification of Germany in 1990 stands as one of the defining triumphs of the modern era — a testament to the courage of Germans who never wavered in their pursuit of freedom. That legacy continues to anchor the enduring partnership between our two nations.

This year, as the United States marks the 250th anniversary of its independence, we are reminded of how deeply intertwined our histories have become. Generations of Americans and Germans have helped shape each other’s nations, which today remain bound by strong shared interests. We additionally welcome Germany’s continued investment in its defense capabilities, a reflection of the clear-eyed understanding that peace and sovereignty must be safeguarded, not assumed.

As we look ahead, the United States reaffirms its commitment to working alongside Germany in pursuit of a safer, stronger, and more prosperous future for both our peoples.

Congratulations again to the Federal Republic of Germany and to all the German people on your National Day of Unity.

item.title: United States and Japan Extend Science and Technology Agreement Indefinitely
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

United States and Japan Extend Science and Technology Agreement Indefinitely

Media Note

October 2, 2026

Today in Tokyo, the United States and Japan signed a protocol that extends and amends the U.S.-Japan Agreement on Cooperation in Research and Development in Science and Technology, also known as the U.S.-Japan Science and Technology Agreement. Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Michael Kratsios signed for the United States and Minister for Foreign Affairs Motegi Toshimitsu signed for Japan.

First signed in 1988, the Science and Technology Agreement provides a legally binding framework for scientific cooperation between the U.S. and Japanese governments. Under this framework, the United States and Japan have built countless links between their scientific communities.

The protocol extends the Agreement indefinitely, a sign of the deep trust and respect between the U.S. and Japanese governments. The extended and amended Agreement positions both countries to sustain and strengthen their cooperation, with a focus on critical and emerging technologies that improve the lives of both peoples.

The indefinite extension reaffirms the long-term U.S. and Japanese commitment to close partnership on science and technology, while advancing a secure, trusted innovation ecosystem that benefits both nations.

item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Horii
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Horii

Readout

October 2, 2026

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met today with Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Iwao Horii, building on the momentum of President Trump’s meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in New York on September 22. The Deputy Secretary and the State Minister recognized the importance of the U.S.-Japan Alliance and their commitment to regional peace and stability. They discussed continued cooperation in the Pacific Islands, including development and infrastructure projects, in support of a free and open Indo-Pacific region. The leaders also reaffirmed their shared commitment to enhancing economic security in other regions of mutual interest.

item.title: Ad-Hoc Coalition to Defeat ISIS Meeting on Iraq and Syria
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Ad-Hoc Coalition to Defeat ISIS Meeting on Iraq and Syria

Media Note

October 2, 2026

Italy hosted, and co-chaired with the United States, an ad-hoc Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS/Daesh meeting of Political Directors and senior diplomatic officials in Rome on October 1, 2026.

Coalition partners congratulated Iraq and Syria on the success of Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR) in degrading ISIS/Daesh. The ending of OIR’s mandate in Iraq represents true victory of the collective efforts of the Coalition and the resolve of the Iraqi government to continue its responsibility to ensure the group cannot regenerate. In Syria, we celebrate the Coalition having a partner in Damascus that recognizes the ISIS/Daesh threat and is determined to work with the Coalition to diminish it. Lasting security in both countries will depend on strengthening inclusive, sovereign state institutions capable of representing and protecting all communities who can equally partake in their country’s future.

Participants reaffirmed the Coalition’s role as a tool for strengthening Iraq and Syria’s stability and that international support should focus on enhancing both countries’ abilities to develop their capacity to target ISIS/Daesh and to prevent the grievances and divisions that ISIS/Daesh has historically exploited. Coalition members expressed their readiness to work closely with the Syrian and Iraqi governments to accomplish this and announced commitments totaling more than 75 million dollars towards supporting Syrian counterterrorism needs, and increasing detention capacity, sustaining health and sanitation services, and supporting displaced and detained populations for both Iraq and Syria.

The Government of Syria highlighted key counterterrorism priorities and gaps for international support and Iraq reaffirmed its ongoing leadership to defeat ISIS/Daesh.

item.title: Joint Statement on the Anniversary of the Snapback of UN Restrictions on and Related to Iran
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Anniversary of the Snapback of UN Restrictions on and Related to Iran

Media Note

October 2, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, Albania, Argentina, Australia, Austria, Bahrain, Belize, Bosnia, Bulgaria, Canada, Colombia, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic, Estonia, Federated States of Micronesia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liberia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Marshall Islands, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Palau, Panama, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, The Netherlands, Trinidad and Tobago, Ukraine, United Kingdom, and Yemen.

Begin Text

On September 27, 2025 (at 8:00 p.m. EDT), six United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs) – 1696 (2006), 1737 (2006), 1747 (2007), 1803 (2008), 1835 (2008), 1929 (2010) – returned into force pursuant to the completion of the snapback process. France, Germany, and the United Kingdom initiated this process in response to Tehran’s persistent and significant non-performance of its nuclear commitments under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).

One year on, we, the Proliferation Security Initiative (PSI)-endorsing States listed above, affirm our commitment to the continued implementation of all relevant obligations enumerated in the reinstated UNSCRs. We further recall that the 2003 Statement of Interdiction Principles (2003), which all PSI participants have endorsed, affirms our adherence to all relevant international law and frameworks, including the UNSCRs.

We further commit, consistent with our UNSCR obligations, to continue to take measures – consistent with relevant domestic and international authorities and related commitments – to prevent the supply, sale, or transfer to Iran of items, materials, equipment, goods, and technology that could contribute to proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities or the development of nuclear weapon delivery systems, as well as to uphold the restrictions on the supply, sale, or transfer of arms and related materiel to or from Iran.

Our countries further reaffirm our commitment to ensuring sufficient domestic legal authorities and capabilities to address Iran’s proliferation-sensitive activities. More concretely, we commit to (1) undertake effective measures to prevent the direct or indirect sale, supply, and transfer to and from Iran of items from or through their territories that could contribute to weapons of mass destruction, their means of delivery (including UAVs), and related materials and items subject to the reinstated UNs arms restrictions; (2) adopt streamlined procedures to facilitate the rapid exchange between PSI partners of relevant information concerning Iran’s proliferation activities; (3) where needed, continue to keep our national legal authorities under review to ensure the effectiveness of our measures; and (4) take appropriate specific actions in support of interdiction efforts related to Iran’s proliferation activities.

We welcome all national-level efforts to implement our UNSCR obligations, as well as relevant activities that support our objective of preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, such as those linked to Operation Economic Outcast.

We urge all UN Member States to implement these resolutions and reiterate the international community’s longstanding concerns about Iran’s nuclear program. We will continue to coordinate our counterproliferation efforts to counter any attempts by Iran to undertake UNSCR-prohibited efforts to resume development of its nuclear or ballistic missile programs. We call on Iran to return to compliance with its nonproliferation obligations, and cooperate fully with the IAEA, and address the international community’s proliferation concerns.

End Text

item.title: United States Cuts Off Hamas Financing Network
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

United States Cuts Off Hamas Financing Network

Press Statement

October 2, 2026

Today’s designations by the U.S. Department of the Treasury target a Hamas military operative in Gaza and a France-based fundraising network that used sham charities and cryptocurrency to collect nearly $2 million for Hamas in recent years.

This action underscores the enduring U.S. commitment to dismantling Hamas’s global support networks and denying the group the resources it needs to plan and carry out terrorism that threatens the security of Americans, our partners, and the broader Middle East. It reflects close coordination between the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, and the FBI to expose how Hamas exploits humanitarian and charitable structures abroad to disguise terrorist financing as legitimate aid work.

The United States will continue working with partner governments, including France, to identify and hold accountable individuals and organizations that provide Hamas cover to raise and transfer funds internationally. Disrupting these networks is central to broader U.S. efforts to isolate Hamas, protect the integrity of legitimate humanitarian assistance to Gazan civilians, and support conditions for lasting regional stability.

We are committed to ensuring that humanitarian aid can be delivered by reliable and safe organizations that advance legitimate Palestinian interests and lasting peace in the region.

Today’s designations were issued pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886, the United States’ core counterterrorism sanctions authority. On October 31, 2001, the U.S. Department of State designated Hamas pursuant to E.O. 13224 for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals, or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States. Hamas is also designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.
